clue.text: Man of God supposedly leaving — settle on replacement

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are put on replacement, swapped about into a new order

explanation.surface: A priest is said to be quitting, and someone is asked to agree on who takes over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on replacement' is the anagram signal for LEAVING SETTLE; 'supposedly' is part of the definition, a dig at preachers whose godliness is doubtful.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcast preacher claims to serve the Lord, and the clue's 'supposedly' casts doubt on his sincerity.

clue.text: Bowled over to England openers last month — new technique picked up

parts.note: the opening two letters of England

indicators.note: in a down entry, picking up lifts the words upward so they read in reverse

parts.note: December, the year's final month, shortened to DEC
art is skill or technique

explanation.surface: A cricketer was bowled after England's opening batsmen fell late in the month to some new trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowled over' tempts a cricket reading alongside England's openers, but it means enchanted; 'picked up' signals the upward reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: To be bowled over is to be captivated or spellbound, which is the participle's sense.

clue.text: Degrade what a Norseman did in speech?

indicators.note: the phrase is spoken, so the sound rather than the spelling counts

parts.note: a Viking oarsman rowed his longship, so 'he rowed', said with a dropped H as 'e rowed

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about how a Viking would be described as behaving.
explanation.walkthrough: Said with the H dropped, as in casual British speech, 'he rowed' becomes 'e rowed.
explanation.definitionFit: To wear away or wear down gradually is to degrade, as a coastline does under the sea.

clue.text: Writer propping up bar as a kind of exercise

indicators.note: in a down entry the piece below props up the one above, so it comes second

parts.note: Aero is a British chocolate bar
a Bic is a ballpoint pen

explanation.surface: A writer leans on the bar, as if drinking were a form of exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: AERO is a well-known British chocolate bar full of bubbles; BIC is a brand of cheap ballpoint pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerobic workouts, such as jogging, raise breathing and heart rate, so the word describes a type of training.

clue.text: Reach hotel passing through South's traditionally impoverished areas

indicators.note: the hotel letter passes through the middle of the phrase for reach

parts.note: to reach a place is to get to it
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
S is the abbreviation for South

explanation.surface: Travellers reach a hotel while journeying through the poorer parts of the American South.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghettos are run-down urban districts where a poor or minority group has long lived.

clue.text: Footballer previously not inclined to give maximum effort

indicators.note: the flat word comes earlier, before the player's name

parts.note: level means flat, with no slope
George Best was a famous Northern Ireland and Manchester United footballer

explanation.surface: A footballer who once seemed unwilling to put in full effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing one's utmost, trying as hard as possible, is the idiom's sense.

clue.text: Letter writer occupied by government flip-flopping

indicators.note: a flip-flop is a turnaround, so the whole assembly is read backwards
the writer's name is occupied by, holding inside, the government letter

parts.note: Martin Amis or Kingsley Amis, English novelists

explanation.surface: A letter-writer complains about a government that keeps changing its mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occupied by' puts G inside AMIS to give AMGIS; 'flip-flopping' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the eighteenth character of the Greek alphabet, so a letter.

clue.text: Dodgy polaroids safe? Happiness short-lived

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or broken, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Instant photographs kept in a dubious safe bring only fleeting pleasure.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a contentment built on illusion, which cannot last once reality intrudes.

clue.text: Neither funked playing different role in theatre

indicators.note: the letters are playing about, jumbled into another order

explanation.surface: Neither actor shirked their part on stage when cast in a new role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatre' is an operating theatre, not the stage: the patient plays a different role there.
explanation.definitionFit: Being operated on by a surgeon is a patient's part in the operating room.

clue.text: Senseless getting Serco, you said — maybe give someone else the job

parts.note: knocked senseless is out cold

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters could be arranged otherwise, so they are jumbled

parts.note: the letter U is said like 'you'

explanation.surface: A jibe that you were mad to hand the contract to Serco, a firm that runs outsourced public services.
explanation.walkthrough: Serco is a British company running outsourced government services, which makes the surface sharp.
explanation.definitionFit: To contract work out to an external firm instead of doing it in-house.

clue.text: Star name following a particular diet

parts.note: Vega is a bright star in the constellation Lyra

explanation.surface: A celebrity is named as sticking to a special diet.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who eats no animal products at all keeps to a strict plant-based regime.

clue.text: Let's wish leader gone

indicators.note: the leading letter of the word is gone, removed

parts.note: as in 'do as you wish' or 'do as you please'

explanation.surface: A proposal to wish the leader would go.
explanation.definitionFit: To let a property is to rent it out under a contract, which is the verb's sense.

clue.text: PM accepts a sign something's wrong following b___ difficult woman

indicators.note: the rest comes after, following the single letter

parts.note: the letter B, shown as a blanked-out word

indicators.note: the prime minister's name accepts, takes inside, the other letters

parts.note: Clement Attlee was the UK prime minister 1945-51
a cross marks an error on schoolwork

explanation.surface: A prime minister puts up with a censored expletive from a troublesome woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'b___' looks like a censored rude word but just gives the letter B.
explanation.definitionFit: An aggressive, domineering woman is the colloquial sense of this insult.

clue.text: Trump's around providing a little bit of 'culture'? I kept trying to calm down

indicators.note: the word for trump is turned around, read backwards

parts.note: to cap is to trump or outdo

indicators.note: the letters for providing and culture keep the I between them

parts.note: if means providing, on condition that

indicators.note: just the opening letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A jibe at President Trump's lack of culture, with someone trying to keep their temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Peacemaking, soothing or conciliatory; the adjective describes an attempt to calm things.

clue.text: Emotionally detached, as football stadiums this year, completely empty inside

indicators.note: the extracted letters go inside the phrase for spectator-less grounds

parts.note: in 2020 games were played behind closed doors, so the grounds were fan-free

indicators.note: emptying a word removes all but its outermost letters

explanation.surface: As detached as football grounds this year, utterly empty during the pandemic.
explanation.definitionFit: Unattached, not in love with anyone, free of romantic ties.

clue.text: During lecture deliberately overlook deception

indicators.note: in a lecture words are heard spoken, so a soundalike is wanted

parts.note: to slight someone is to snub or pointedly ignore them

explanation.surface: A lecturer who deliberately ignores trickery in the room.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight of hand is trickery or cunning dexterity.

clue.text: Good landlord won't rent — place now empty

parts.note: a pub landlord is the host

indicators.note: rent means torn apart, so the letters are pulled into a new order

explanation.surface: A decent landlord refuses to let property, so the area becomes deserted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like the landlord's income but is the past participle of rend, to tear.
explanation.definitionFit: A deserted settlement whose inhabitants have all left.

clue.text: Army personnel backing Queen stand around

indicators.note: the royal letters are backing, going in reverse

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina

indicators.note: the letters move around into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Soldiers supporting the Queen stand about.
explanation.walkthrough: Army ants march in vast columns; the definition's 'Army' is insects, not soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ants live in colonies and some species march in great columns, so they form an insect army.

clue.text: Pampered, wanting nightcap initially sent up

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so a letter is missing

parts.note: a spoon-fed child is pampered

indicators.note: the opening letter of nightcap is the one meant

explanation.surface: A spoilt person goes to bed without a bedtime drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To send up is to parody or mock, which is also to hoax or lampoon.

clue.text: Issue 100 in book for adult students?

indicators.note: the number goes in the middle of the book phrase

parts.note: a tome from the OU, the Open University, which teaches adults by distance learning
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A query about whether an issue of a hundred copies suits mature learners.
explanation.walkthrough: The Open University (OU) is Britain's distance-learning university for adults.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue is a result or consequence, as in the issue of a matter.

clue.text: Look up info about King — you'll easily get cash for it

definitions.text: you'll easily get cash for it

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means reading the word upwards, in reverse

parts.note: lo means look

indicators.note: the information word goes about, around, the king letter

parts.note: dope is information, the inside story
R, Rex

explanation.surface: Researching a king's details turns out to be easy money.
explanation.walkthrough: From the British idiom 'money for old rope', meaning money earned for almost no effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy money comes from something worthless, as in the saying about selling worthless leftover cord.

clue.text: Dry wit rarely Oscar's way? I shouldn't say this

indicators.note: rarely, used oddly here, signals the letters done unusually, jumbled

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
RD, road

explanation.surface: Was arid wit seldom Oscar Wilde's style?
explanation.definitionFit: A taboo term, one considered unmentionable, which a speaker should not utter.

clue.text: One going through most of shop's correspondence

indicators.note: the numeral goes through, inside, the trimmed phrase
most of means one letter is dropped from the end

parts.note: to shop someone is to rat on them
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone passing through most of a shop's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A proportion between quantities is a correspondence in size or amount.

clue.text: Submit — it's Vlad!

definitions.meaning: to ... an application or claim is to submit it
Vladimir ..., Russia's leader, shares the setter's pseudonym

explanation.surface: An order to surrender because Vlad has arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: Hand in a form or a bid; and Russia's president, named Vladimir.

clue.text: Immature creatures are protected by others

indicators.note: the letter is protected by, wrapped in, the word for the other young

parts.note: pups, other immature creatures, young dogs or seals
an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated A

explanation.surface: Young animals are sheltered by older ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects in the chrysalis stage between larva and adult are not yet mature.

clue.text: What makes music fresh — it's live, mostly

indicators.note: fresh suggests a new arrangement of the letters
most of the word is used, losing its last letter

parts.note: to live is to be, and 'are' is a form of be

explanation.surface: Musing on what gives live music its freshness.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indian stringed instrument with a long neck, so a source of tunes.

clue.text: Sure can — fellow returned piano to top of house

indicators.note: returned means going back, reading the two pieces in reverse

parts.note: the can and the loo are both slang for a toilet
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
the roof is the top of a house

explanation.surface: A man came back and moved the piano up to the attic.
explanation.definitionFit: Certain to succeed because it cannot go wrong even if mishandled.

clue.text: Might relish habitually doing this to impress?

parts.note: power and might both mean strength
a dressing is a sauce or relish

explanation.surface: Someone who enjoys showing off by their routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habitually' puns on habit as clothing: dressing in a habit to impress.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearing smart business clothes to look authoritative at work.
